name: WSC(Winograd Schema Challenge)
intro: WSC（Winograd Schema Challenge）是一个常识推理基准，使用特定的Winograd语义结构题。题目包含一个歧义代词，需根据句中某个词正确指代先行词，考验模型的世界知识和推理能力。
build_method: 人工标注, 专家构建
intro_en: WSC (Winograd Schema Challenge) is a common-sense reasoning benchmark that uses specific Winograd semantic structure questions. Each question contains an ambiguous pronoun that must be correctly resolved to its antecedent based on a word in the sentence, testing the model's world knowledge and reasoning ability.

drawio_review_note: Aligned with Levesque, Davis, and Morgenstern, The Winograd Schema Challenge, KR 2012, Sections 4-6 and 8 for the constrained schema criteria and proposed native-speaker/hidden-challenge protocol; Kocijan et al., A Review of Winograd Schema Challenge Datasets and Approaches, arXiv:2004.13831, Section 2.1 for the WSC285/WSC273 version relationship; official NYU benchmark catalog https://cs.nyu.edu/~davise/Benchmarks/Text.html and hub https://cs.nyu.edu/~davise/papers/WinogradSchemas/WS.html. Version pin: WSC273 is the first 273 examples of the 285-example benchmark snapshot; it is shown separately from the paper's proposed future hidden challenge and is not claimed to have passed that proposed empirical protocol.. KR 2012 defines a constrained Winograd schema as a pair of sentences differing in one or two special words, with an ambiguous pronoun whose correct antecedent reverses between the two variants. Ideal candidates are obvious to ordinary human readers, resist selectional-restriction shortcuts, and are Google-proof against simple corpus statistics. The paper proposes empirically testing future candidates with normally abled native English-speaking adults before admitting them to a hidden challenge corpus; that proposed acceptance gate must have both pass and revise/reject outcomes. Separately, the expert-authored original benchmark snapshot grew to 285 examples. WSC273 is the first 273 examples, excluding the later 12, and is evaluated as binary antecedent selection with accuracy. The diagram does not claim that all WSC273 examples passed the paper's proposed future native-speaker protocol.
